key_insight: The paper proposes replacing objective-led trial and error with invariant-based solution construction when sufficient problem structure is available.
engineering_relevance: For nonlinear engineering problems, the framework aims to enable interpretable, directly constructed solutions rather than statistical compromises.
method: Deconstruction: suspend prior assumptions and disentangle coupled units.
Structure: extract rigid invariants intrinsic to the problem.
Construction → Solving: build invariant-anchored equivalent mappings, execute them, and verify results afterward.
evidence_signal: The abstract cites demonstrations in number theory, Hamiltonian systems, deep learning, and seismic inversion, but reports no quantitative benchmarks or evaluation details.
watch_item: Practical value depends on identifying sufficient invariants and valid equivalent mappings; when structure is insufficient, the framework falls back to objective-driven optimization.
paper_title: The Four-Element Theory of Structure-Driven Methodology: A Methodological Shift from the Perspective of Natural Science and Engineering Practice
